Dear *Waylon Van Dieman,* 





Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *4 May 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *All rides history*



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-za/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-za/privacy/?category=rides|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Hi Amin,

Thank you for your response and for explaining the current priorities regarding cloud services. I understand the emphasis on using AWS for new developments due to its standardized platform and robust features. However, for the specific needs of my current project, access to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is critical, particularly due to its seamless integration capabilities with Google Sheets.

The core requirement of my project involves automating data transfer directly into Google Sheets. While AWS offers extensive services, it lacks the native integration that GCP provides with Google Sheets through Google APIs. These APIs allow direct manipulation and management of Sheets without complex workarounds, making development straightforward and more efficient.

Moreover, setting up authentication and data handling between AWS and Google Sheets involves additional layers of complexity and development time. It requires configuring AWS Lambda functions to handle OAuth authentication with Google APIs, managing API Gateway for secure data transmission, and ensuring data format compatibility. These steps, while feasible, introduce potential points of failure and increase the maintenance overhead.

GCP, being part of the Google ecosystem, offers out-of-the-box solutions for interacting directly with Google Sheets, which significantly simplifies the process. This direct integration is vital for ensuring that our solution is both robust and easy to maintain, especially given our use case's reliance on real-time data processing and reporting in Google Sheets.

Given these considerations, having access to GCP would be instrumental in efficiently achieving the project's goals. It would allow us to utilize Google's native tools and ensure that we can maintain high standards of reliability and user experience without additional overhead.

I hope this clarifies the necessity of GCP for our specific needs. I am open to discussing this further and exploring any possible alternatives you might suggest that could meet our project requirements within AWS if absolutely necessary.

Thank you for considering this request.

Best regards,

“Dear Melyssa,

Thank you for your letter dated 18 April 2024.

We have reviewed the AASA’s request and regret to inform you that Bolt cannot sign the proposed Data Processing Agreement (DPA) for AASA suppliers, as it does not accurately reflect the business arrangement between Bolt and AASA, nor the legal roles of Bolt and AASA as far as data processing is concerned. 

As you know, when providing services to our Bolt business customers, Bolt autonomously determines the means (how the data is processed) and purposes (what is done with the data) of personal data processing as a responsible party under POPIA, corresponding to the status of an independent data controller role under the GDPR. Our [General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business|https://bolt.eu/en-za/legal/?category=boltBusiness], specifically *Section 4,* reflect that both Bolt and the business customer operate as separate data controllers (responsible parties), each accountable for their respective data processing activities and compliance with applicable laws, including POPIA. More specifically, the Ts&Cs state that “_Bolt and Customer all adhere to all the applicable data protection laws, e.g the General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (GDPR), including application of proper technical and organizational data protection measures. Bolt processes personal data as described in Bolt’s Privacy Policies. All available at_ [http://bolt.eu/en/legal/|http://bolt.eu/en/legal/|smart-link]  _as applicable in the relevant territory, and as may be amended from time to time._”

While we appreciate that Sections 20 and 21 of POPIA set out requirements that AASA’s operators must abide by, these do not apply to Bolt and therefore AASA is under no legal obligation to bind Bolt by AASA’s DPA. However, Bolt is required to comply with Section 19 of POPIA, which sets out applicable security measures on integrity and confidentiality of personal information — our Bolt Business Ts&Cs cater for this already.

We appreciate your attention and trust that this explanation clarifies your concerns with regard to our refusal of the proposed DPA.

Kind regards,”

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *30 April 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and

*Your rights*

You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Dear Pamella Qasana

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *30 April 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

Total projected yearly spend is 744,000€ - 4,800€ (120,00 CZK) = *739,200 €*

Hi [~accountid:5df3830c73b0bd0e4d835499] , picking this up. 
Am I correct in understanding that the concern is that Swedavia will be able to piece together Bolt’s city market share and then share this data with third parties?

The privacy clause 5.7 is directed at personal data (data of Drivers etc.) and does not cover any business data. There is however a confidentiality clause in the agreement (clause 13) which states that neither party may disclose to third parties information that can be considered a trade secret. By my initial assessment Bolt’s market share can be qualified as a trade secret under Swedish law (namely under [§ 2 of the Trade Secrets Act|https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/lag-2018558-om-foretagshemligheter_sfs-2018-558/#:~:text=%C2%A7%202%20%C2%A0%C2%A0In%20this,for%20the%20owner.]) and therefore Swedavia is prohibited from sharing this data with third parties. If Bolt is in a position to request amendments to the agreement, then, for clarity’s sake and risk mitigation, clause 13 could be amended with a non-exhaustive explanation on what is included under trade secrets within the context of the agreement.

However, if the concern is based on the sharing of personal data then this ticket should be assigned to the Privacy Team.

Let me know your thoughts.

Best,

Dan

Usually how this works is:

Riders book rides offline via specific telegram channels that advertise Bolt 50% Off Rides 👉 [https://t.me/taxi5001|https://t.me/taxi5001|smart-link] 

# Channel owners send a payment request to the riders
# Riders pay
# Channel owners phish driver numbers via the above in app message
# They request the driver to go to a specific location where there is no supply so as to assign a ride to them (usually a long trip) and agree on a price stating the above or that they work with Bolt as a travel agency that allocates rides
# They request an in app €10 ride, our system preauthorizes it successfully
# Ride is allocated to that specific driver since no other drivers are close and available
# Driver accepts, goes to agreed pickup location, picks up riders, takes them from or to the airport or from to another city
# Driver ends ride with a PR for the amount they agreed on whatsapp
# Driver gets paid by Bolt, Bolt has a failed payment
# Driver initially thinks all is fine until the system triggers a fraud detection and we investigate
# There are also drivers who are directly collaborating with them knowingly.

That should sum it up more or less. Do you need any more info?

Hey [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d]! I’ll answer below. Please let me know if you need any more info.


* Can you please advise what the ETA is for launching this feature? _A 50-50% percent AB test has already been running from the 24th of April. We will rollout the feature to all users (with new-ish app versions and devices) around a month after the test started._
* Is this only for iOS or Android as well? _iOS and Android_
* I see that passkey would be one of the ways to log in to the account, not the only one, eg we *propose to create a passkey, not require.* _Correct_
** Am I correct that we would still provide a way to sign up with a phone number? How would we solve recycled phone number cases with this please? _Yes, users will still be able to log in with a phone number, passkeys are just another authentication method that they can use. Passkeys do not provide a fix for recycled phone number cases_
** How much people do you expect would use passkey? _We don’t know this yet, the technology is quite new. We expect mostly tech-savvy users will use it in the beginning, so a relatively small percentage of users._
** Would we propose a creation of a passkey for logged in users, not only those who sign up or logged out (and try to log in). _Yes, we will propose it to all users who have a new-ish app version and device_
* Can you please describe the flow for this: when the user wants to sign up, we propose to create a passkey. _We only suggest creating a passkey after the user signs up. Users needs to be logged in in order to create a passkey_
** Is this passkey being created on a user device independently from Bolt or is all happening in the Bolt app? _The passkey is created and stored on the user device by the device OS itself, not in the Bolt app. Bolt app only receives and stores an id of the passkey and a public key for decoding the sign in requests. The passkeys created for Bolt cannot be used on any other application._
** Once the key is created, is this stored in iOS/Android device, eg we do not have any information regarding the passkey? _Bolt only stores an id of the passkey and a public key for decoding the sign in requests._ 
* When the user wants to sign in with a passkey, what is the flow? Do we retrieve the passkey from a device or do we match the passkey we have and the user presents? _Upon opening the Bolt app (unauthenticated):_
** _Bolt backend generates a random challenge and sends it to Bolt app_
** _Bolt app asks the device OS if the user has any passkeys stored for the Bolt app. If it does, the device OS signs the challenge using the passkey’s private key (which is only stored on the user device by the device OS)_
** _If the user has a passkey for Bolt and the challenge was signed, Bolt app sends the signed challenge + passkey id to Bolt backend_
** _Bolt backend identifies the passkey by id, checks the signed challenge (using the passkey public key that was stored when creating the passkey) and signs in the user associated to that passkey_

** The original payment method button will be available without taken into account what was happening with bolt balance refund.
** Order is 10 eur, rider accepted 6eur refund to bolt balance, but then asks for giving him money to his card. In such a situation, agent can make partial card refund for 6eur to not refund the whole 10 euro.
* The main rule is that it is possible to refund to card at max how much money user paid by card.
* When rider accepts the bolt balance refund, the ticket gets closed and if they want a refund to the org. payment, they would need to create a new ticket.
* Partial option in "original payment method refund" will always lead to refund only to card, and partial option will not allow making a refund bigger than money paid by card. So if it is needed to make a full refund for split order, agent will need to select "full" option.
** If the rider paid 2eur by card and 8eur by bolt balance, and we need to make a full refund - if we select the original payment method, the 2eur will go to card and 8eur to balance. And if we select full refund to balance - 10eur will go to balance.

Hey [~accountid:6140b8db805a97006aa66cc8] 

I have now had a chance to review this ticket. Thank you for taking the time to explain this ticket during our call. You explained that the business intend on recalculating downwards in situations where the Fraud Team have flagged habitual patterns with drivers, these patterns are when drivers are not picking up passengers, starting the trip, driving a short distance and then completing the trip (known as ‘ghost trips’). This then results in the passenger being charged the full fare and the driver being paid out the full fare even though the trip did not occur. Bolt then has to refund passengers for the trip, which is resulting in a loss for the business and a poor customer experience. 

I have now reviewed the General Platform Terms for Drivers and the Fraud Policy. The terms and conditions explain that Bolt is permitted to withhold payments from drivers when fraud has occurred and if the drivers behaviour is considered as ‘prohibited behaviour’. See the relevant clauses below: 

+*GENERAL PLATFORM TERMS: DRIVERS*+ 

# Acceptable Use Policy

b. You must not and you must ensure that all other Service Providers using the Bolt Platform in association with your account must not:

iii. {color:#bf2600}modify, interfere with, disrupt or hack the Bolt Platform{color}, including introducing any software viruses or {color:#ff5630}use the Bolt Platform to commit any fraud against Customers, the Bolt Parties or any third-parties{color} (like credit card issuer, holder, etc.);

7(c). {color:#ff5630}Not complying with the Acceptable Use Policy is a serious breach of these Terms {color}and will entitle Bolt UK to take any of the following actions (with or without notice, subject always to Section 9):

i. {color:#ff5630}immediate, temporary or permanent withdrawal of your right to use the Bolt Platform{color};

ii. immediate, temporary or permanent removal of any User Content;

iii. {color:#ff5630}issuing a notification to you{color};

iv. legal action against you, including proceedings for reimbursement of all costs (including, but not limited to, reasonable administrative and legal costs) resulting from the breach;

v. {color:#ff5630}withholding or permanently denying any payments payable to you as a result of prohibited behaviour that does not comply with the Fraud Policy.{color} In these circumstances, your right to appeal such a decision is set out in the Fraud Policy; or

+*FRAUD POLICY*+

# Prohibited Behaviour

Behaviour that will be considered by Bolt to be Prohibited Behaviour is set out below:

3.1. {color:#ff5630}providing or allowing (including any attempt to provide or allow) any inaccurate, misleading, duplicate or false Information to the Bolt Parties, the Bolt Platform and/or any Users relating to the provision, carrying out, time, duration or location of any service requested or provided via the Bolt Platform{color};

# Bolt’s expectations of Users and consequences of Prohibited Behaviour

4.1. {color:#ff5630}Users must not participate in (or allow) any Prohibited Behaviour{color}.

4.2. {color:#ff5630}User access to the Bolt Platform may be suspended or terminated if Bolt suspects, considers or determines at its discretion that there has been a failure to comply with this policy{color}.

4.4. {color:#ff5630}Service Providers are reminded that, in accordance with the terms and conditions that apply to them, Bolt may delay payments that would otherwise be due to Service Providers on the basis that Bolt is investigating a failure to comply with this policy{color}. Bolt also {color:#ff5630}reserves the right to permanently deny payments{color} to Service Providers {color:#ff5630}where such payments relate to Prohibited Behaviour and Bolt has determined that there has been a failure to comply with this policy{color}.

+*TO SUMMARISE*+ 

* The General Platform Terms for Drivers and the Fraud Policy (relevant sections outlined above) allow Bolt to withhold payments from drivers if suspected fraud has occurred, therefore the business can recalculate downwards where ‘Ghost Rides’ have occurred. 
* It is important that when the business start recalculating downwards and/or withholding payments from drivers that drivers are allowed the right to appeal, this is outlined in Section 7(v) of the General Platform Terms for Drivers,{color:#4c9aff} {color}which says:

v. withholding or permanently denying any payments payable to you as a result of prohibited behaviour that does not comply with the Fraud Policy. {color:#ff5630}In these circumstances, your right to appeal such a decision is set out in the Fraud Policy{color};

In addition to the right to appeal outlined in section 7(v) of the General Platform Terms for Drivers, section 6 of the Fraud Policy says the following: 

+*RIGHT TO APPEAL IN FRAUD POLICY*+

# Appealing a decision relating to this policy

6.1. Users will not be permitted to appeal a decision by Bolt to terminate a User’s access to the Bolt Platform in accordance with this section 6 if Bolt determines at its discretion that the failure(s) to comply with this policy are so material and/or persistant that it warrants immediate termination of a User’s access to the Bolt Platform. When this is the case, it will be made clear in the relevant Statement of Reason.

6.2. Other than in the circumstances set out in section 6.1 above, the relevant User will have 30 days from the date of issue of a Statement of Reason to appeal any decision by Bolt to suspend and/or terminate any access to the Bolt Platform in association with the User’s account. In order to appeal this decision, the relevant User must promptly appeal the decision with reference to the applicable Statement of Reason, providing Bolt with such additional Information it may request in relation to the Statement of Reason from time to time. Appeals should be made in writing and as instructed by the Statement of Reason.

6.3. Bolt will consider all appeals in good faith and will reinstate any suspended access to the Bolt Platform (and release any temporarily suspended payments to Service Providers) as soon as reasonably practicable from the date that Bolt determines at its discretion that:

6.3.1. there has not been a material failure to comply with this policy; or

6.3.2. other circumstances apply that make it fair and reasonable to reinstate access to the Bolt Platform.

6.4. If, after the expiry of the 30 day period set out in section 6.2 above, Bolt at its discretion still considers that the User has participated in (or allowed) the Prohibited Activity referred to in the Statement of Reason, Bolt will be entitled to terminate the User’s access to the Bolt Platform in accordance with the terms and conditions that apply to the User.

Taking into account the replies received, I would say that the MY legislation focuses on broad taxing rights, so in line with other developing countries analyzed. The definition of royalties still seems to be taken in a broad manner, so it is worthy to ask them to confirm their position that the payment for access to our app is equivalent to the OECD view on payment for the use or right to use. I shared this remark in the slack channel, as the file has a weird formatting.

It is also important to ask if the broad view of tax authorities is confirmed or reversed by courts.

Here is my exact analysis:

"I would still question them on the view that Bolt will receive royalty payments due to the intermediation. They refer to the payment as royalty because it is for the use or right to use the app, but I would point to the OECD commentaries on article 12, mainly paragraphs 13 and 14, to question that. I would argue that Local subsidiary is not paying for the copyright in the app, but rather for having access to the software as such, so it is as a payment for a copyrighted product.

But considering their remark on tax authorities trying to tax the payments as royalties because service is provided via the Bolt App, I would ask whether MY follows the OECD Commentaries and if there is case law on the matter (one thing is for tax authorities to view the payment as royalties, a different one is whether courts favour this view - There might still be judges in MY”

Idea of the story is:

# Developers create a {{bolt-server/deploy/package/foo/README.md}} file that contains information useful during package releases - e.g. links to dashboards, runbooks, procedures
# On package release, the Builder pipeline page will show this information

Questions:

*Q1: Where to display this information?*

A: On the pipeline page, but the actual UX is out of scope for this clarification. Throwing out some ideas:

* We need to render the content for each package in the release
* It should not be weird when we have both {{prelive}} and {{live}} releases for the same package (i.e. not duplicate content)
* Content can be large and difficult to fit into the release dashboard; we already have some data to display there and can easily become cluttered
* For these reasons, I’m inclined to suggest putting a link (maybe just an emoji) close to the package name. This will open a modal panel showing the {{README.md}} contents

*Q2: How to load this information*

A: README contents should be loaded from the {{gitrepo/bolt-server}}repo on the Builder worker’s disk. Given that a pipeline is bound to a single worker, the file system info should be consistent throughout the pipeline’s lifetime.

README contents to display should be loaded from disk during the {{ReleaseReadyUserValidation}} step (the one which builds the release dashboard). There was an alternative idea to load the contents and store them on the pipeline info (build_action), but this could increase the size too much in case there are many packages in the release.

Builder UI should use a markup renderer to make the README contents pretty when displaying them.

h3. Alternative quick implementation

A super easy way to (partially) handle the user request would be to hard-code a link to the README location in GitHub. We have the branch ref, so we can link to the current version that’s being released.

Downsides:

* We’ll generate links to nonexistent READMEs if the package does not have one
* We’re not actually “showing” the README contents, but it’s just 1 click away

Implementation would be trivial.

Hi Taisiia,

There’s more to unpack here.

But briefly: 

* we use e-mail addresses in profiling rules. These rules are automated and work in the background, so we can and do actually take action on users based on related suspicious activity across an e-mail address.
* e-mail addresses are very easy to switch. In most day to day analysis, even if we pick up a pattern based on an address, or get an individual request about a suspicious one; it won’t be a very good long-term solution as fraudsters tend to pick up on what’s stopping them and if they can, they will change that detail on their account.
* I’m not sure how the fraud graph helps in Safety training - but in general,  from the fraud side, we don’t want to encourage CS agents to use the graph to detect fraud. Often times, they see a graph with a lot of connections and they reach out to us because they find it suspicious. However, if the users are connected through the graph, then we’re already seeing all these connections, we have rules in place to detect suspicious activity across all connecting elements, and there is no need for escalating to us for manual investigations.
* I don’t think that e-mail addresses will be added as a connecting element to the graph. If there is a strong business case for this from the Safety perspective, I recommend conducting a separate analysis and providing your findings. But this would take engineering work and can cause confusion for other CS agents referring to the graph.

I hope this helped clarified things, but don’t hesitate to respond here if you still have questions.

Best,

Francesca

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

From the engineers:

I believe the applicable scenario is this: we auto-archive accounts when certain conditions are met in order to protect users' accounts and data.

Linking the product guide: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/4359225370/Phone+number+recycling+Account+archival+Email+OTP|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/4359225370/Phone+number+recycling+Account+archival+Email+OTP|smart-link] 

But, here’s the TLDR on why and how:

Every time you change your mobile phone number, your carrier will recycle your previous number. They 'recycle' the number by assigning it to a new phone and corresponding customer. The carriers report doing this in order to avoid 'number exhaustion,' or a situation where all possible numbers have already been used for each mobile phone.

Since *Bolt user accounts are identified only by their phone number*, if we didn’t have any protection against it, the following situation could happen:

* John owns the number {{+1234}} and creates a Bolt account with it
* John changes phone number to a new one {{+5678}}
* Jane inherits John’s old phone number {{+1234}} from phone number recycling.
* Jane downloads the Bolt app. Asked for her phone number, she inputs {{+1234}} and verifies it.
* Jane is logged in to John’s account

!72.png|width=72,height=72,alt="😧"!

This is a privacy and security risk that we want to prevent.

*Account auto archival* leverages the *grace period* that phone carriers use before they decide to recycle a phone number (6 months in most countries).

In a nutshell, when there is a sign-in attempt into an account, if:

# The user has not opened the Bolt app for at least as long as *the* [*grace period defined*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/4359225370/Phone+number+recycling+Account+archival+Email+OTP#How-long-is-the-grace-period-for-phone-recycling%3F] *for his phone number extension* (e.g. +372 for Estonia);
# The device that is trying to log in has never logged into this account before;

Then we assume they could be a different person and do not log them into the existing account. Instead we:

# *Create* a brand new account associated to the phone number to take its place and log the user into it;
# *Archive* the account that was previous associated to that phone number.

_The decision whether to archive an account doesn’t happen by itself. It happens_ *_only when there is a new authentication_* _into the account in question, using phone verification (not Google/Facebook Sign-in)._

Hello Zip,

Thanks for your comments and here are the answers to your questions:

# Should O7926 be a negative amount as it is a refund?

Ideally yes, but from Billing side we have invoice_type to define if it is a refund or driver invoice, thus we put all values in positive to make sure all data follows the same rules. You can filter invoice_type to find refunds and set them to negative manually.

# What cause the difference between Orders and Invoices and Summary?

As I can see your formula of Sum with VAT per tab "Summary" (deduct refund 9,000) takes in_app order price(from old admin) + in_app order price(new admin) + cash order price(new admin) - Refund. In this calculation you didn’t include cash order price from old admin, which is 308,180. The correct way to use Summary tab to sum up all ride price should be B30+C30+L30+M30, while the first 2 columns represent old admin, the latter for new admin. The additional 9,000 discrepancy is because in Orders and Invoices report, the refund is shown in positive value and you don’t need to deduct it twice.

# What cause the difference between [+Ride Hailing - Rides Report 2024-04-15T1554+|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R3QCJo7BPrIpPGilj4VPSe1czVM9Bxgm/view?usp=share_link] and Orders and Invoices tab, Which ride report should be sumbitted?

This discrepancy is because in Orders and Invoices tab we try to match data between invoices and balance. As all invoices are generated on local timezone, while Balance is shown in Tallinn timezone, thus we removed 15 records that were generated after 23:00 06/30 from the Rides report, in order to find the discrepancy to Balance report. When submitting, you can use the report extracted from Looker.

# From my side, I would also not recommend collecting the user’s docs via the Google forms and store them in Gdrive. 
## The Google forms are not a best practice process for document collection due to privacy concerns and the way these documents are scattered around the GDrive.
## All docs collected from users should be stored in Admin, so we have a centralised team (Identity) that is responsible for creating retention periods for the documents, ensure access is limited to certain employees, security measures required by the InfoSec are implemented and other requirements are easily made by one team without the need to look for all people who can control these docs
## Our team needs to have a data inventory where we understand where data is stored and how it’s used. Creation of different G Drives and Forms creates frictions for us and make it difficult to control this.
## Moreover, as Bolt is obliged under the privacy law to disclose the user’s data to users in case they request it, our team or the CS would not be able to remember all the locally managed folders to get this data. We are aiming at centralising the approach so all the data are stored in Admin and the data owners are clearly identified.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Our requirements for collecting user’s documents*

# We should stick to the same approach we use across all verticals. Afaik, we use *Formaloo* for collecting driver’s and courier’s documents, eg I would suggest we use the same provider/form for collecting user’s documents.
## This form allows the docs to be moved to Admin.
# We should be able to store these docs in Admin profile of the user so these documents are easily accessible from the profile and user ID.
# We should NOT collect these docs via Beehive or personal devices of our employees: the collection of documents should be secure and reliable, eg as pointed out above, the data owner should be the Identity team.
# If we want to use a 3rd party provider, our team would need to assess the data collected, the privacy and security practices of this provider along with the InfoSec team as per our supplier assessment process and give a green light for this provider (if it’s a new one or extension of services with the existing one)
# All the personal data of users should be deleted from work or personal computers of our employees. Of course, sometimes we need to download them to our computers to send it out, but we should aim to delete all these docs from personal computers.

For audit trail and to summarise the support given:

1] Due to late notice and time constraints, the participants of the event were first verbally informed that the event can be photographed;

2] After this, the legal team must followup with {{Authorisation agreement to use image rights}} + {{PRIVACY NOTICE}} to the participants asking for their consent to use the images. If the consent is not received, the photos and supplementary data will be deleted.

3] The privacy team has flagged the following risks to the stakeholder:

* the reason why we ideally needed to avoid verbal notification before the event when the photos are taken - we ideally need a clear *proof* of consent and/or notification *before* the photos are taken. Obtaining consent verbally and/or verbal notification does not guarantee this. 
* This is especially important when vulnerable groups are concerned, i.e. people with disabilities, as we are at risk of processing special categories of personal data (health) - which has very stringent consent and recording requirements under the GDPR.
* Bolt does not consider processing special categories data in this case, as the purpose of the activity is not to infer any special categories of data in photos (i.e. racial origin, health - disabilities, religious beliefs) from the data subjects.

More information on support can be accessed in the parent ticket.

Hi Taisiia,

There’s more to unpack here.

But briefly:

* we use e-mail addresses in profiling rules. These rules are automated and work in the background, so we can and do actually take action on users based on related suspicious activity across an e-mail address.
* e-mail addresses are very easy to switch. In most day to day analysis, even if we pick up a pattern based on an address, or get an individual request about a suspicious one; it won’t be a very good long-term solution as fraudsters tend to pick up on what’s stopping them and if they can, they will change that detail on their account.
* I’m not sure how the fraud graph helps in Safety training - but in general, from the fraud side, we don’t want to encourage CS agents to use the graph to detect fraud. Often times, they see a graph with a lot of connections and they reach out to us because they find it suspicious. However, if the users are connected through the graph, then we’re already seeing all these connections, we have rules in place to detect suspicious activity across all connecting elements, and there is no need for escalating to us for manual investigations.
* I don’t think that e-mail addresses will be added as a connecting element to the graph. If there is a strong business case for this from the Safety perspective, I recommend conducting a separate analysis and providing your findings. But this would take engineering work and can cause confusion for other CS agents referring to the graph.

I hope this helped clarified things, but don’t hesitate to respond here if you still have questions.

Best,

Francesca

# *What does the setup look like now*

Currently, even if a fleet’s Invoicing strategy is Company (payouts are, in reality, made to Fleets' bank account, not to drivers' personal bank accounts), the company details are *not* synced on driver profiles in Driver Portal and Admin/Admin Panel. Instead, drivers' personal payout details are shown. This can cause confusion for both drivers themselves (as payouts are not made to the bank details linked on their profile, but to their Fleet Owner who will then re-allocate the funds to the fleet’s drivers) as well as Bolt employees (for the same reason).

it would be efficient to have the fleet details be automatically synced to fleet driver profiles as long as Invoicing strategy is Company. That way driver profiles will automatically reflect accurate payout info (Fleet’s, as opposed to driver’s).


# *How will the change precisely look - what data will be displayed, where (fleet portal? driver app? rider app?) and to whom (riders? fleet? Bolt only?) will it be displayed*


*What data:* Payout, billing, tax details

*Where:* Driver Portal, Admin/Admin Panel

*To whom:* Fleet data will be shown fleet drivers in the Driver Portal, and to Bolt in Admin/Panel on the fleet drivers' profiles

Hey Mark, 

Our Support Solutions Team is working in updating the workflow to clarify such uncertainties 🙌 Hopefully in 1-2 months they will be able to launch the revamped workflow. 

For high and significant cases it is the first step to call the user, after checking all details in Beehive (message & order) and reading correct SOP.  Even if you do not need more info, you still call to ensure the user is given support  from our end. 



The scorecard is referring to vague cases vs. clear cases but the call for high/significant still comes first. It’s more to highlight that even these one liner reports like “Driver touched me” are still a clear report and we should act on it. 

In the past, people had the tendency to wait to log a report until the reporting party gave more info, or until the reported party replied but that should not be the case. 



For vague cases, indeed the case handling is kind ofthe same, you reach out to get more info, if the user doesn’t answer, you write them. Based on the expected severity, you follow up within the 24h/48h timeframe. The big difference is not opening the tool or tagging it as safety + de-escalation and closing as a Tier 1 case if you don’t get a reply. 



Regarding the reply to the reporting party. If the ticket is still open then the agents can indeed close it. If they would’ve been able to close the ticket earlier (eg. the reporting party provided all info, call was clear), then they do not need to keep the ticket open until the very end.

* Optimized query from the development team

{noformat}SELECT ub.id,
	   ub.master_basket_id,
	   ub.last_booking_id,
	   ub.city_id,
	   ub.user_id,
	   ubb.state                   AS booking_state,
	   ubb.type                    AS booking_type
  FROM user_basket AS ub
  LEFT JOIN user_basket_booking_state_log AS ubbsl
	   ON ubbsl.user_basket_booking_id = ub.last_booking_id
  LEFT JOIN user_basket_booking AS ubb
	   ON ubb.id = ub.last_booking_id
  LEFT JOIN (
	     SELECT MAX(id) AS max_id, user_basket_booking_id
	       FROM user_basket_booking_state_log
		  WHERE city_id IN (1, 325, 326, 1153)
		  GROUP BY user_basket_booking_id
	   ) AS ubbsl2
	   ON ubbsl2.user_basket_booking_id = ub.last_booking_id AND ubbsl.id = ubbsl2.max_id
 WHERE ub.last_booking_id IS NOT NULL
   AND ub.state = "authorizing"
   AND ub.last_update > DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 2 DAY)
   AND ub.city_id IN (1, 325, 326, 1153)
   AND ubbsl.created < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 2 SECOND)
 LIMIT 10;{noformat}

This is not about whether the driver’s location was there or not. If they ended up at the estimated destination in Estonia then *they did an offline trip* with the customer as there was no active journey nor tracking. Essentially in Bolt’s eyes, there was no order active on that journey as *the journey through Bolt platform was ended in* *_Brīvības gatve 372_*. And this cannot be a mistake by touch as upon order finish the driver has to slide to finish the ride as well as as an extra step to confirm the final price. Please be reminded that it is imperative for us to have trip records and tracking, and if they proceed with an offline journey this not only goes against our T&C but *also is a potential threat to our licence*. 

Please be advised that if the app refuses a destination change it is for good reason - Bolt is not allowing the route to be adjusted or extra destinations to be added - and upon that happening the driver should finish the journey and another journey needs to be placed if need be.

* DS won’t be measured by the numbers anymore, as it’s legally risky - _the drivers may ask where did it go_
* Automatic blocking for DS won’t be relevant anymore in the high-risk markets; the Drivers get blocked only after a manual review by the Local OPS. * Drivers will be able to see compliments _-_ positive reviews by the riders in the app _- drivers may share feedback on it, so the CS should know about the feature_
* We can no longer externally refer to it as "Driver Score" - comms to teams and heads up to quality to check this. Drivers will be blocked only based on the contextual blockings, but never based on a "general blocking".

Dear Tazul Islam

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *10 May 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Trip details of specific trip on 04/05.24*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Hi the team,



{{The issue}} is that we disclose the personal data of drivers (name, surname and tax ID number) on such invoices. We received advice from data protection lawyers in UA and they concluded that Bolt does NOT have a right to disclose personal data of drivers on invoices as there is no any law that obliges drivers to issue invoices to riders with their personal data. No legal basis available in UA apply to this activity.

{{What does it mean?}}
We have  agreed with the CM and relevant people to delete tax ID from invoices and leave only first name (without any further details of the drivers).

{{Risks:}} if one of the drivers decides to lodge a complaint to the Commissioner on human rights in UA, the Commissioner would send a formal letter to us asking to explain why we do so. In this case, they can require us to shut down the process or propose other solutions as well. The penalty can also be imposed.

Hey [~accountid:5f155fa05ee2c30023a32dc1], I think we need to understand the differences here:

# The rider fell asleep in the car and the driver was taking a detour to increase the price - distance fee increased - Driver at fault
# The driver was stuck in traffic - wait time fee/traffic congestion fee increased - Driver not at fault
# Driver taking a longer route due to incident on the road -  distance fee increased - Driver not at fault
# Driver missing a turn and ending up on the highway - distance fee increased - Driver at fault



_Also, when rider complains that the price went up due to traffic, we don’t refund,_ [_following this process_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012406780]_._

Got it, however in that case, I would make [this split |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/5739607795474]more granular. If we cannot scale it to all the events, the wording there is IMO misleading, as it implies that the driver is at fault under all overcharging circumstances

_What’s more, if we refund from driver’s earnings for the longer route and later driver reaches out saying that the refund is unfair - we can compensate the driver_ [_following this process._|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010660613#a-recent-trip-was-refunded]

They need to go to the balance to notice this; we’re not making it easy to appeal against the deduction. Additionally, It creates additional volumes and therefore adds cost

_So I still think that for longer route the refund actor should be driver, and the manual compensation to driver shouldn’t be issued right away (unless the driver contacts us and explains what actually happened)._

Hi [~accountid:637f26822acfad92d7b13ddb],

Filling in whilst Sandra is on annual leave. If I understand correctly, the problem statement that you are referring to here - is that sometimes in Telema you can have fields which are either empty, or have incorrect combinations and you want to enforce an error/send-back via the integration to notify AP team of this? 

If my understanding is correct, then we need to review where the specific problems are. There are two sides to any of the end-to-end processes that we have: functional and technical.

Functional means the business usage of the tools that we use, and how we can build systems/processes to prevent errors, automate processes and aid specialists. This is the point is whether in System A (Telema) or System B (Workday) we handle these exceptions, validations. Functionally to define what type of data we accept, what is required, what is allowed combination and so on. This is where we define user guides, data entry, processing and so on.

Technical means executing code that moves data from System A to System B. Integration/Code should always move data from one system to another and by a principle design rule should never manipulate data - as that has risks, and is against generic programming principles as well as well as internal controls.

Therefore - if the data entered in Telema allows the process/invoice to be sent to flow - and then picked up by integration then the integration will move the data from A to B. Given that the data meets the required fields, it will create the invoice and try to submit it. If there is a problem with cost center (maybe inactive, wrong combination etc) - then it will go into draft and error mode. 

So, if validation is not able to be done on Telema side from what I understand, then it needs to be done on the Workday side and invoice needs to be handled in Workday. This is in synch of what I have been trying to advise on - to use Workday as a centralized invoice processing system to ensure validations, approvals is in one place - whilst still using Telema for the basic information.

So please confirm whether my understanding is correct, and whether any additional validations need to be built on the Workday side to aid the process. I understand it may be inconvenient to edit draft invoices in Workday, so let’s try to simplify the process where possible.

Hi Janeli, 

Sure, will explain in a bit more detail - and make sure we’re on the same page. If you have an example of an invoice, where the error did occur/did not occur - then please let me know, ping me via slack before it’s “fixed” manually, so we can look at the direct case.

In general data is entered into Telema. Invoice is received, AP enters the coding from the available values, and sends it to flow. Once it’s approved, it’s ready for transfer.

The integration that is built by the Integrations Team, takes whatever invoice data is in Telema, then loads it into Workday. If the relevant invoice information - supplier, company, payment terms exist in Workday and the line level information exist - cost center, business line, region, spend cat etc then it will create the invoice. It will then submit it in Workday, and invoice will be in APPROVED state. 

 If let’s say there is a new cost center that is in Telema, and not in Workday - the integration won’t be able to find that cost center and will return an error to state ERP complained. 

If however let’s say you use a business line of scooter, on a cost center of rides - then that is a functional validation that would be done in Workday. It is not something that the integration does, or should validate on it’s own. 

If there is an incorrect combination of dimensions/tax then the invoice will be created in draft, as the validation will prevent it from being submitted. 

So TLDR:

* Validation will only pull data from Telema, if the relevant values are in Workday - it will create this invoice. 
* If there is an issue with combinations, so invoice gets created in draft, that has to be corrected by accountant/AP specialist in Workday.

revoked or not, cert is still in the table
there’s 2 different things 
end-entity = user data/user
cert = the actual certificate 
when you do revoke, only cert status changes in the table, and when you remove end entity with revoked cert, entity is removed but cert is still there, that’s the core purpose of the ca - tracking certs.
so in total > 
end-entity can be removed but not revoked
certificate - can be revoked but not removed
and the outcome will be different,  depending on if you’re removing end entity with already issued certs or not

[~accountid:712020:477677eb-f20d-49e9-b662-304d1440db6f] Cool. Just sharing few things in general which you might already know:

* When you say 1rem in figma it is converted to a CSS px by multiplying it to root node font-size (In our case, it is 16px). This means if we change this, every value that we defined will automatically get changed.
*  A CSS pixel different from any hardware pixel (for Example you Full HD monitor may have 1920x1080, but not be 1920px wide in terms of CSS pixel). 
* A CSS pixel is exactly the same size in physical world sense, i.e 1/96 of an inch (atleast it is supposed to work like that in modern browsers). So a font-size defined in terms of CSS pixel will always be same size in real world sense, no matter what screen you look at. 
* For raster things such as images, canvas etc, browsers first create a bounding box by calculating the amount CSS pixels, which means a fixed physical size independent of screen size and then paint it based on the screen’s actual resolution.


PS: This is all assuming 1x zoom. The accessibility scaling settings works like pinch zoom and works on top off everything else.

In my opinion, Polish wording of the actual T&Cs allows Bolt to terminate the agreement without any reason with a 30 day notice, while point 8.3 discussed with DP does not include such possibility. Bolt will be entitled to terminate agreement only if a breach by DP occurs.  On the other hand, we agree in the special terms that the Agency Fee may not be changed unless agreed by both parties. Consequently, lack of possibilities to terminate the agreement and to increase the fee by Bolt uniterally may result in Bolt’s obligation to provide services for a non-market fee for an unknown time (until DP terminates agree itself). I amended this clause to it allows Bolt to terminate the agreement without a cause.

Hey,

The bank details are collected/not collected depending on local driver registration setup/flow, this is configurable on market level.

But it is best to collect personal payment details as well as:

* Fleet drivers can sign up without having joined a fleet, and being matched later on in the process. So we do not know always the relevant fleet’s invoicing strategy at the time the driver signs up
* Fleet company’s invoicing strategy may change so we should store the personal bank details as well
* Fleet drivers often move between fleets (invoicing strategies of source and target fleet which may differ)

So for deleting the already existing data, I don’t think it would be wise from operational POV. The idea is more about visually removing misleading payout details from driver profiles in Admin + Driver Portal. So personal details should not be displayed if payout is done to Fleets directly.

And this is my bad. But looks like actually, the preferred scenario would be that: *No payout data is shown on driver profiles (in Admin and Driver Portal) for fleet drivers if Fleet Company data is used for payouts.*

Hey!
Currently we rely on Local teams to identify parts as damaged once they receive them from CWH and to notify us or FAEs. 
Most of the time, the damaged parts get notified to the COPS Inventory team during the Inventory Count week.

When this happens, the damaged parts gets either Quick Issued or quantity adjusted via Inventory Count Sheet’s approval.
In both cases, the costs associated to the spare parts impact the PnL of the country where the damaged parts are received.

In the link in my original message, the NL team raised the issue against OKAI IOTs, each of them costing 72 EUR. Each unit received damaged, has a very big hit in their profitability.

I would like to find a way to divert the cost associated to this from a Local PnL to a central one, if that makes sense from a financial point of view.



*How I think the process should look like*:

* We should identify which items should be included in this process (example, I would include IOTs, Controllers, Motors, Forks, non-swap batteries [items which can be checked from remote or are very expensive], but I would exclude Kickstands, Brake levers, Cables etc).
* We should have a prior assessment (from HW team maybe?) to identify the actual malfunctioning of the part(s).
* Once that is confirmed (by HW team?), COPS Inventory team would perform the Adjust Inventory task.



By excluding smaller and less expensive parts, we would not encourage Local teams to use this opportunity incorrectly and solely for their benefit.

By including a prior assessment of the damage, we could avoid misdiagnoses (like it happened with Torque Sensors, for example).

By allowing only COPS team to perform Adjust Inventory, we would be sure the task is used as intended.



Please let me know if you need extra inputs!

Thanks

“United Kingdom
Report from our correspondent Richard Curtis, Tax Author
Tax Authority Publishes Information on Registration for Pillar Two Taxes

The UK tax authority, His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC), has published information on how to register to report Pillar Two top-up taxes.

The United Kingdom has two Pillar Two taxes. The domestic top-up tax (see Part 4 of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2023) may apply if the company or group is located only in the United Kingdom. The multinational top-up tax (see Part 3 of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2023) may apply if the group has entities located inside and outside the United Kingdom – in which case the entity must register for both Pillar Two top-up taxes.

Companies or groups of companies must register for Pillar Two top-up taxes if they have at least one entity located in the United Kingdom and have consolidated group annual revenues of EUR 750 million or more in at least two of the previous four accounting periods. Such companies must register, regardless of whether a Pillar Two liability arises or not, no later than 6 months after the end of the group’s first accounting period that started on or after 31 December 2023.
Registration must be made by one group member on behalf of the whole group. The default position is that the parent entity will register, but another company may do this if nominated by the parent entity. The first returns of Pillar Two taxes must be submitted no later than:

30 June 2026, if the first accounting period for Pillar Two top-up taxes ended on or before 31 December 2024; or
18 months after the last day of the group’s accounting period, if the first accounting period for Pillar Two top-up taxes ended after 31 December 2024.

Links to further information and contacts can be found on the HMRC website here.

Registration can be done here and after registration the entity can use their Government Gateway user ID and password to sign in and manage their account.

Note that this service is being introduced on a phased approach and tools to enable returns to be submitted will be released before the due date for reporting. Also, agents cannot register for this service on behalf of groups – if they have authority to manage Pillar Two top-up taxes they must sign in to their agent services account.

The HMRC guidance published on 20 May 2024 is available here.”

”_Report from Dr René Offermanns, Principal Associate, IBFD_

Belgium Issues Pillar Two Notification Form

On 21 May 2024, the Belgian tax authorities provided practical guidance regarding a Pillar Two notification obligation for multinational enterprises and large-scale domestic groups with consolidated annual revenues exceeding EUR 750 million in 2 of the 4 previous fiscal years. Once registered, the authorities will issue a specific Pillar Two identification number (P2 TIN) that taxpayers will need to use for Pillar Two advance tax payments, reporting and compliance.

_Notification Requirement_

Taxpayers must perform the notification by filing the P2 Notification Form. Thereafter, they can make Income Inclusion Rule (IIR) and Qualified Domestic Minimum Top Up Tax (QDMTT) advance tax payments and submit Pillar Two related notifications and tax returns. The P2 notification form must be filed by:

|–|the Belgian ultimate parent company if there is only one ultimate parent entity established in Belgium;|
|–|the Belgian ultimate parent entity designated as agent if there are several ultimate parent entities established in Belgium;|
|–|a Belgian group entity if there is no ultimate parent entity and only one group entity is established in Belgium; and|
|–|the Belgian group entity designated as agent if there is no ultimate parent entity and multiple group entities are established in Belgium.|

_Terms_

Multinational enterprises and large-scale domestic groups that fall within the scope of Pillar Two must file the P2 Notification Form within 30 days of the reporting year's start. However, companies already in or about to begin their first reporting year will benefit from a deadline extension of 45 days.

_Content of the Notification_

Taxpayers must disclose the following information:

|–|Part I – Information related to the multinational enterprise or large-scale domestic group, which includes:
–    
the name of the multinational enterprise group or large-scale domestic group;
–    
the start date and end date of the reporting year, with the earliest possible start date being 31 December 2023;
–    
the address of the UPE establishing the Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) for Pillar Two purposes, including street, number, postal code, municipality, and country (ISO code);
–    
the phone number, fax number, e-mail address and hyperlink to the corporate website (all optional);
–    
the type of entity and legal form being either an 'organization without legal personality' or a 'foreign entity';
–    
details of the individual representing the UPE, including first name, last name, Belgian National Register number or the so-called BIS-number which is a unique identification number for (foreign) individuals not registered with the Belgian National Register;
–    
the capacity of the multinational enterprise group/large-scale domestic group (pre-populated field);
–    
the nature of the group, being either a multinational enterprise group or large-scale domestic group; and
–    
confirmation whether the group constitutes only one legal entity (or not).|
|–|Part II – Information related to the CFS of the multinational enterprise or large-scale domestic group, which includes:
–    
type of CFS of the UPE (as defined under Article 10 of the OECD Model Rules or as implemented in domestic law);
–    
the accounting standard used for the CFS the UPE, including the corresponding ISO code; and
–    
the ISO code of the currency used for the CFS of the UPE; and
–    
the information related to the publication of the CFS of the UPE online (hyperlink) or confirmation that the CFS are not published online.|
|–|Part III – Information related to the ownership structure of the multinational enterprise or large-scale domestic group:
–    
the name, jurisdiction (ISO code) and TIN (in line with the OECD tax identification number structure);
–    
the GloBE status, which includes constituent entity, flow-through entity (tax transparent or reverse hybrid), hybrid entity, permanent establishment, main entity, minority-owned parent entity, minority-owned subsidiary, minority-owned constituent entity, investment entity, joint-venture, joint venture subsidiary, non-material constituent entity, excluded entity, ultimate parent entity, partially owned parent entity and intermediate parent entity;
–    
type of excluded entity if applicable: governmental entity, international organization, non-profit organization, pension fund, investment fund that is a UPE, real estate investment vehicle that is a UPE, entity owned by an excluded entity;
–    
if applicable: constituent entity, minority-owned subgroup, standalone minority-owned constituent entity, investment entities, joint venture group, stateless constituent entity;
–    
the TIN of the entity on top of shareholding structure of the sub-group (if applicable);
–    
the consolidating entity for Pillar Two purposes;
–    
information regarding the UPE or UPE's (Belgian or foreign) if the UPE is Belgian, the part 3 information should be provided for all Belgian and foreign entities under the UPE;
–    
information regarding the Intermediary Parent Entity or Entities (Belgian or foreign);
–    
if the Intermediary Parent Entity is Belgian, the above information should be provided in this subpart for all the Belgian and foreign entities per Belgian Intermediary Parent Entity;
–    
information related to a Partially Owned Parent Entity or Entities (POPE) (Belgian or foreign); and
–    
if POPE is Belgian, the above information should be provided in this subpart for all Belgian and foreign entities per Belgian POPE information related to any other entity established in Belgium.|
|–|Part IV – Information related to the enterprise to be contacted:
–    
name of the filing enterprise acting as point of contact of the group for the creation of the Belgian P2 TIN;
–    
tax identification number, jurisdiction, and address of the enterprise; and
–    
the name of the contact person within the enterprise and the E-mail address and phone number of this person.|

_Format_

Taxpayers must register with the FPS Finance by submitting a P2 Notification Form, in XML format, that will be made available on the digital government platform "MyMinfin". When submitting this file, taxpayers will need to confirm the following items:

|–|start- and end-date of the reporting period;|
|–|whether the company wishes to make use of P2 related prepayments;|
|–|the actual XML file, together with the (PDF) mandate form; and|
|–|the Contact e-mail address.|

Thereafter, the FPS Finance will register the multinational enterprise or large-scale domestic group with the Belgian trade register and send the specific Belgian P2 TIN for the group. The full text of the guidance is available [+here+|https://financien.belgium.be/nl/actueel/pillar-2-opening-systeem-verplichte-notificatie] (in Dutch) and [+here+|https://finances.belgium.be/fr/actualites/pilier-2-ouverture-systeme-notification-obligatoire] (in French).

Finally, figure out with jfrog support what’s going on. So they have 2 versions of DB Sync mechanism, v1 and v3. 

DB Sync v3 is just a newer version with some other algorithm, the only diff, is that DB Sync v1 runs every 24 hours, while V3 runs every 1 hour. These mechanisms also provide different metrics and APIs. 

The thing is, that DB Sync v3, is used as default in versions higher than 3.80.x, BUT only in case of clear installation on this version. Upgrade to the latest version, doesn’t bring this functionality….

So the only way to switch from V1 to V3, is to:

* Fully terminate xray and DB of xray. 
* Install it again with any version higher than 3.80.x. 

OR

* Jfrog in theory may prepare some instructions, and need to execute a bunch of commands on the DB side to migrate to V3.  

----

Currently, there is a choice, between how to solve the problem, or to re-install xray prelive to get V3 or re-install xray live to get V3. 

On one side V3 is a newer mechanism, on the other:

* From jfrog support words, it doesn’t relate to scans, just how to sync DB 
* All documentation that I found on jfrog side related to DB sync of V1, no information about DB Sync v3 at all, possible to get something about it only via contact with support. 

So from a maintenance perspective more straight way is to re-install prelive to have DB Sync v1 (due to it more stable) in both place. If in one day jfrog announces it’s globally and left v3 sync only as one recommended, pretty sure it will be some official instructions how to do it without termination of all the data.

With [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/100758|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/100758|smart-link]  merged we can now see what is actually going on

Here’s an example: [https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/HVFxV|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/HVFxV] 



!image-20240523-100026.png|width=50%,alt="image-20240523-100026.png"!

Right before the CBs open we see a lot of {{TTL exhausted!}} messages. These come from [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/27a1ea8941ba85ba9f892985fc3e080d285eda80/src/router/internalRequest/InternalRequestClient.ts#L573] and happen whenever the available caller TTL is exhausted even before the http call to the client is requested. Which means that the calls are not even reaching {{migrateToAddressForm}}.



*Why does the TTL exhaust?*

Unknown yet. The working theory is that sometimes the Elasticsearch queries issued by {{delivery-order-locations}} take too long and by the time we reach the point to call {{migrateToAddressForm}} there will be no more time available. Will test this theory out by adding some {{@timedAsync}}s to the ES queries.



*Why are the CBs opening?*

The code [right now|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/9aee4969845f86f8d7a6bb1a014fde0702f4c581/src/delivery/geo/delivery_order_locations/main/service/DeliveryOrderService.ts#L192] involves calling {{migrateToAddressForm}} in parallel, for each of the addresses in the “top delivery address” list. If the TTL is already exhausted (or close to being exhausted) by the time we execute the {{RunParallel}}, _all_ of the requests will “fail” (some of them might not be even issued). This produces a large number of errors in a short period of time from the same host (this is is the same reason the InternalRequestClient logger gets throttled), which can trigger the CBs.



*Why don’t we see the timeouts in Prometheus?*

Because the Prom counters are not incremented by NJSC for this flow 🙃 These are incremented [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/27a1ea8941ba85ba9f892985fc3e080d285eda80/src/router/internalRequest/InternalRequestClient.ts#L616], in {{finalize()}}, which is not invoked in case of TTL exhaustion.

 

*More on TTLs*

The timeout value set by the {{getUserTopDeliveryAddresses}} endpoint is 110 ms. However, {{location-suggestions-delivery}} configures a 500 ms value when invoking this endpoint. One would expect that {{getUserTopDeliveryAddresses}}’s TTL to be 500 ms. It is not. As stated in the [documentation|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3666116815/GUIDE+TTL#How-TTL-is-set], the value is determined by taking the minimum b/w the endpoint TTL and the caller TTL.

Przedsiębiorca nie może naliczać konsumentowi opłat w wysokości nadmiernej w stosunku do poniesionego kosztu (np. nadania korespondencji), gdyż rażąco narusza to interes konsumenta.

Koszty te powinny być ustanawiane w cenach rynkowych, przy uwzględnieniu zasady, zgodnie z którą konsument nie może zostać obciążony kosztami prowadzenia działalności przez przedsiębiorcę.

[Globalne warunki korzystania z elektrycznych hulajnóg Bolt (obowiązują od 12.04.2023 r.) | Bolt Legal|https://bolt.eu/pl-pl/legal/terms-for-e-vehicles-new/?category=micromobility]

5.6.1. zostanie zaparkowany poza Dozwolonym Miejscem Parkingowym, możemy obciążyć Użytkownika kwotą opłaty za odbiór w wysokości do 100 EUR (do 460 PLN). Kwota ta wynika z kosztów ponoszonych przez Bolt w związku z odbiorem Pojazdu Elektrycznego i powiązanymi kosztami,

5.6.2. będzie nosił ślady uszkodzeń wykraczających poza normalne zużycie, będzie znajdować się w złym stanie technicznym lub będzie zdewastowany, możemy obciążyć Użytkownika kwotą stanowiącą równowartość kosztów naprawy lub wymiany Pojazdu Elektrycznego i wyposażenia,

5.6.3. zostanie porzucony bez uprzedzenia, Użytkownik będzie odpowiedzialny z tytułu wszelkich opłat do czasu odzyskania Pojazdu Elektrycznego, plus opłata za poszukiwanie w wysokości do 120 EUR (do 560 PLN) oraz maksymalna opłata za korzystanie z Pojazdu Elektrycznego, wskazana w Aplikacji, zależnie od czasu, który upłynie do momentu odzyskania Pojazdu Elektrycznego, kwota ta wynika z kosztów ponoszonych w związku z odbiorem Pojazdu Elektrycznego i powiązanymi kosztami,

5.6.4. nie zostanie odzyskany lub zwrócony (tzn. jazda zostanie zakończona, a Pojazd Elektryczny – zaparkowany) w terminie 48 godzin, możemy uznać, że Pojazd Elektryczny został utracony lub skradziony, w którym to przypadku możemy obciążyć Użytkownika opłatą w wysokości do 500 EUR (do 2350 PLN) od Pojazdu Elektrycznego oraz zgłosić dane zdarzenie na policję.

5.6.5. nie zostanie zaparkowany zgodnie z punktem 3 Regulaminu Jazdy i co nie zostanie potwierdzone wyraźnym zdjęciem z zakończenia jazdy, gdy został o to poproszony w Aplikacji, możemy nałożyć na Użytkownika opłatę w wysokości 6 EUR (30 PLN) ("Opłata za Naruszenie Zasad Parkowania"). Nieprawidłowe parkowanie Pojazdu Elektrycznego lub niezrobienie wyraźnego zdjęcia zakończenia jazdy w celu umożliwienia weryfikacji zaparkowania Pojazdu Elektrycznego przez Użytkownika stanowi naruszenie niniejszej Umowy i nałożenie Opłaty za Naruszenie Zasad Parkowania jest uzasadnionym i koniecznym środkiem mającym na celu zapewnienie właściwego użytkowania parkingów, przestrzeni publicznych oraz bezpieczeństwa i wygody innych użytkowników i członków społeczeństwa.

5.7.3. Jako rekompensatę za koszty poniesione w związku z przetwarzaniem spraw naruszeń Użytkownika na podstawie pkt. 5.7, Bolt ma prawo pobrania rozsądnej opłaty administracyjnej, która nie przekroczy 30 EUR (140 PLN). Opłata administracyjna nie zostanie pobrana, jeśli w procesie wyjaśniania sprawy okaże się, że Użytkownik nie ponosi odpowiedzialności lub jeśli nie zostały poniesione żadne koszty. Należne kwoty, o których mowa w pkt. 5.7.2 oraz 5.7.3 będą pobierane przy użyciu Wybranej Metody Płatności Użytkownika, zgodnie z pkt. 5.8.

[~accountid:6012aaf8a41ea5006a613a63] , I did some consulting and the answer should be along the lines:

We only transfer the earnings to the account of the fleet whose drivers made the rides. This mainly stems from our T&Cs (which the fleet has accepted; see clause 6.4.1 of [Allgemeine Geschäftsbedingungen für Personenbeförderungsunternehmen|https://bolt.eu/de-de/legal/tnc-transport-rentals/?category=rides]), but also due to our internal policies. While technically possible, we do not approve such requests due to risk management principles and reporting obligations, as such fleet-to-fleet transfers can be very high risk (essentially - tax evasion).

As such, the request is unfounded and so is the lawyer’s claim, as Bolt is not liable for damages the fleet has carried due to submitting a request that Bolt is not contractually obligated to approve and will not approve due to risk management principles. Therefore, we will not transfer the earnings of Mazhar Farooq Mietwagen GmbH to Iwona Farooq Mietwagen and we will not compensate the lawyer’s fees.

However, this does not effect Mazhar Farooq Mietwagen GmbH’s right to their earnings. Also, Mazhar Farooq Mietwagen GmbH is free to change their bank account details provided on the Bolt Platform, in which case the earnings can be transferred to the updated bank account.

Hi [~accountid:5da0457ec62f840db2b704a9],

Blocking a driver for behavior-related incidents is *not possible* due to legal constraints.

Also, requesting the driver to transfer the money back to the rider is not a viable solution for the following reasons:

* The driver might not respond, resulting in a prolonged resolution process.
* The driver might refuse to issue a refund.
* Agents would need to share the rider's phone or bank account details, posing a GDPR compliance risk.

Considering these factors, the most practical solution would be to *inform users that Bolt is not responsible for transactions made outside of the app and cannot offer compensation*.

Do you see any obstacles to implementing this approach? While I understand this might not satisfy riders, it's important to note that intervening in transactions outside the app and compensating high amounts with promo codes or requesting refunds from drivers carries significant risks.

Additionally, could you please share data on the frequency of this issue in your market? This information would be very helpful.
