* If you have children, proof that they go to kindergarten or school 
* If you have a business in Estonia yearly tax income form 
* Airline tickets that show when you entered Estonia (only applicable if they have a name on it) 

If you provide just employment contract this alone will suffice. But if you provide rental agreement this would need additional documents mentioned in the list above.

Ok, I looked a bit closer into this. Root issue is the following: 

User opens chat → we request header info (but we haven’t yet added any comments to the support case) → We return default header because no comments → We add initial message to support case → webview refreshes → We get correct header information. It all happens quickly so it causes this flickering. 

How I see it we have 2 options to fix this: 

1) {{getLastBoltAgentCommentAuthorInformation}} in SupportCaseService can return no header (no title, no image) when there is no comments. This way user opens chat, we display empty header until we have a comment and only then show Alfred 

2) On webview side we don’t call getHeaderInformation when case messages is empty or undefined

While the outside attorney cannot assess the risks precisely in terms of percentage, below please find a list of the *potential risks arising from the proposed green Tesla project* and general level of risk:

* The TVDE regime prohibits the display of brands and advertising on TVDE vehicles, as these must be uncharacterized. On the other hand, the concept of advertising in Portuguese law is significantly wide. In view of the above, we cannot exclude the *possibility that the color of the vehicles, in itself, falls within the concept of advertising* and, consequently, Bolt can be subject to the sanctions provided for on the TVDE legal regime: (i) *payment of a fine of € 5.000 to € 15.000* and (ii) *ban on the exercise of the activity for a maximum period of two years*. However, the outside attorney estimates this risk as *less than 50%*, namely for the following reasons: (i) there is no other reference to the Bolt brand on the vehicles and (ii) the color is not registered as a Bolt trademark.

* We maintain the risk assessment previously carried out in relation to the *cooperation agreements*:

* In terms of *ride-hailing regulatory risks*, as you know, the TVDE regime prohibits electronic platforms to own TVDE vehicles, or finance or be an interested party in business relating to the acquisition, rental, leasing or other use of TVDE vehicles --> *Bolt's contribution to the purchase of vehicles by the FO is therefore likely to involve a regulatory risk*. The penalty for the *administrative liability ranges between €5,000 and €15,000*, depending on the degree of fault.
* The *decision to interdict activity* is highly dependant on the level of risk that is taken by Bolt. We have no knowledge about prior cases where these measures were applied. Although we cannot exclude the possibility of such measures being applied to Bolt, we understand that this prohibition mainly aims to protect the integrity of the TVDE services and was not thought for the situations as the one in this case. As such, we believe that it is *unlikely* that this deal will create *significant risks* for Bolt as regards the application of any of these measures.
* From a *banking regulatory perspective*, it is *unlikely* that the envisaged agreement with the FOs will be deemed as being in violation of the principle of banking monopoly, because the contribution from Bolt to the FO does not match the characteristics of a professional lending activity, namely it (i) does not correspond to the professional activity of Bolt, (ii) does not include an interest on the principal amount, and (iii) the return on investment is directly linked to growth of business.

* You should also note that both from a banking or ride-hailing regulatory perspective if a penalty is applied to Bolt, the competent authorities may decide to make the *decision public* (e.g. local news).

* Please note that even though this project does not change the risk assessment in relation to the cooperation agreements, *it might trigger investigations and questions from the regulator*. In that case, the regulator will have rights equivalent to authority agents and the *cooperation agreements might have to be disclosed*.

*Things to consider*:

* *gradual roll out* (to see if it attracts the regulator's attention);
* *no public communication / PR on this project* (as this cannot be seen as advertising and we need to ensure this cannot be linked to the cooperation agreements).

Will keep {{delivery-address-form}} endpoints to 3 seconds for the time being.

However, the calling endpoints in {{delivery-order-locations}}  have unreasonably (and unnecessarily) low timeout values, which lead to TTL exhaustion and can cause problems. So the plan is to raise those. A recap:

* {{setDeliveryLocationOrderIntent}} 
** current timeout: 300 ms
** does not invoke {{delivery-address-form}} so *leave it as is for now*
* {{getDeliveryLocationOrderIntent}}
** current timeout: 110 ms
** is invoked by _a lot_ of non-geo clients, most of which do not even care about the address form
** invoked by {{location-suggestions-delivery}} on the {{getDeliveryLocation}} and {{suggestDeliveryLocations}} flows, both of which have a more relaxed TTL
** *raise to 500 ms and consider exposing a “simplified” version of this endpoint for non-geo clients with a lower TTL*
* {{getUserTopDeliveryAddresses}}
** current timeout: 110 ms
** invoked by {{location-suggestions-delivery}} on the {{suggestDeliveryLocations}} flow
** *raise to 500 ms*
* {{getUserInRadiusLocations}}
** current timeout: 110 ms
** invoked by {{location-suggestions-delivery}} on the {{getDeliveryLocation}} flow
** *raise to 500 ms*
* {{getDeliveryOrderAddressDetails}}
** current timeout: 110 ms
** invoked by {{location-suggestions-delivery}} on the {{getDeliveryLocation}} and {{recordDeliveryLocationEntered}} flows
** *raise to 500 ms, and also raise* {{/v2/recordDeliveryLocationEntered }} *timeout to a round value of 1000 ms*

Hi [~accountid:5f155fa05ee2c30023a32dc1], thank you for your reply.

The issue is very frequent issue in our market - as I mentioned, we have had 4 cases this week only that are still on-hold while we figure out the process. 

Most of our drivers are part of a fleet, not private drivers. It’s legal to ask for 350€ for a cleaning fee in public taxis, often fleet cars actually have a sticker inside the car stating this. As the fleet owner will take a cleaning fee out of the fleet driver's pocket in the end of the day if the car is not clean, newer fleet drivers have the pressure to charge passengers outside of the app automatically. Most of them likely don’t read our terms and conditions, thus don’t know it’s against them to charge the cleaning outside the app(some of them have not even submitted a price review ever before).

{quote}Do you see any obstacles to implementing this approach?{quote}

The process in the [🚗 Rider: I was charged more than expected|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012406780#price-review-issues] KB states that we should compensate with prom codes if it’s first time, but only with a cash payment. 

# Most nordic/baltic markets/users use in-app payment to pay for Bolt rides, so excluding compensating those fully really disregards the majority
# Why should the process for in-app payment be any different than for cash payment? We should also be able to compensate at least the leftover amount in promo codes even if the rider paid via in-app.
# The cleaning fee amounts in Finland are just very high(up to 350€) that not compensating equivalent amount to that or at least trying to contact the driver from our side would hurt the market a lot.
# Many drivers would actually be okay with transferring the money back, if we give our word that we will compensate the same amount back from our side. Yes it poses a GDPR risk, but it isn’t any bigger than for example, sharing the passengers phone number wihtin a Lost item case if we have written agreement.
# If let’s say, we don’t receive a concensus with the driver/they don’t answer us, we could always at least provide a full refund like[ the KB currently says|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/115003285874].

Taking all this into account, we collectively feel there should be a better process for compensating the ‘'first-time outside-the-app’' charged cleaning fees. 

*The best possible scenario for in-app payment + rider paid additional cash for the cleaning fee would be to:*

* Contact the driver and convice them to tranfer the amount back + compensate them manually after they do
* If the driver is not willing/does not respond, offer a full refund to original payment method/BB + compensate the rest with either Bolt Balance or promo codes(if BB isn’t possible)

Let me know if any of this would work 🙏

# In case of distro dir (bionic for example) it’s quite easy. We have structure:

{noformat}/bionic/system|other/package_name{noformat}

For package from system repository will be use main components package, for other will be according to the naming.

{noformat}/roles/rsyslog/tasks/main.yaml:    repo: deb <https://debrepo.taxify.eu/debrepo/system/rsyslog> ./

{noformat}

About the script, prepared version for standard distro from APT-S3:

{noformat}#!/bin/bash

function backfill_standard_repos () {
apt_s3_repositories=$1
for repository in $apt_s3_repositories ; do
  # TO DO: It may works for bionic/focal/jammy/trusty/xenial
  # For incoming/other/static/ need to make another block of code
  # TO DO: Don't forget to remove HEAD before applying
  mkdir -p buffer_dir/$repository
  echo ----------------------------------------------
  echo Starting processing repository for $repository
  echo ----------------------------------------------
  AWS_PROFILE=bolt AWS_PAGER="" aws s3 ls  --recursive bolt-apt-s3/$repository > $repository

  deb_packages=$(awk '{print $4}' $repository | grep -E .deb$ | head -n 2)
  amount_of_packages=$(awk '{print $4}' $repository | grep -E .deb$ | wc -l)

  progress=$amount_of_packages

  echo ----------------------------------------------
  echo Total amount of packages for processing is: $amount_of_packages
  echo ----------------------------------------------
  for package in $deb_packages ; do
    if [[ $package == *"$repository/system"* ]] ; then
      component="main"
    else
      component=$(echo $package | awk -F '/' '{print $2}')
    fi

    if [[ $package == *"amd64"* ]] ; then
      arch="amd64"
    elif [[ $package == *"arm64"* ]] ; then
      arch="arm64"
    else
      arch="all"
    fi

    package_name=$(echo $package | awk -F '/' '{print $NF}')
    progress=$(echo $progress-1 | bc)

    echo ----------------------------------------------
    echo Uploading $package_name from S3
    echo ----------------------------------------------

    echo Uploading package to Jfrog with COMP: $component ARCH: $arch DISTRO: $repository

    AWS_PROFILE=bolt aws s3 cp s3://bolt-apt-s3/$package buffer_dir/$repository/ 1> /dev/null

    curl -s -X PUT "<https://LOGIN:PASSWORD@registry.prelive.boltint.net/artifactory/debian-bolt/pool/$package_name;deb.distribution=$repository;deb.component=$component;deb.architecture=$arch>" --upload-file buffer_dir/$repository/$package_name 1> /dev/null
    echo ----------------------------------------------
    echo Migrated to jfrog, left $progress out of $amount_of_packages
    echo ----------------------------------------------
  done
done
}
#Pass as argument here one of bionic/focal/jammy/trusty/xenial to run in parallel
backfill_standard_repos $1
{noformat}
